  21  * Each upgrade step consists of two elements:
  22  *

  24  *    - Data dictionary operations from ADOdb library; one of:

  26  *      AddColumnSQL, AlterColumnSQL, RenameColumnSQL, DropColumnSQL,
  27  *      CreateIndexSQL, DropIndexSQL
  28  *    - InsertData: local function to add data to the db
  29  *    - UpdateFunction: local function to perform arbitrary changes;
  30  *      the function must be defined in install_helper_functions_api.php
  31  *      with 'install_' prefix
  32  *    - null: no-op upgrade step
  33  *
  34  * 2. An array of the parameters to be passed to the function.
  35  *
  36  * The integrity of the schema relies on strict ordering of this array.

  38  *   Always specify the schema step (array key), for documentation purposes

  17 /**

  34 
  35 ##############################
  36 # MantisBT Database Settings #
  37 ##############################
  38 
  39 /**
  40  * Database Server host name.
  41  *
  42  * Hostname should be either a hostname or connection string to supply to adodb.
  43  *
  44  * For example, if you would like to connect to a database server on the local
  45  * machine, set this to 'localhost'.
  46  *
  47  * If you need to supply a port to connect to, set hostname as 'localhost:3306'.
  48  *
  49  * @global string $g_hostname
  50  */
  51 $g_hostname = 'db';
  52 
  53 /**
  54  * User name to use for connecting to the database.
  55  *
  56  * The user needs to have read/write access to the MantisBT database.
  57  * The default user name is "root".
  58  *
  59  * @global string $g_db_username
  60  */
  61 $g_db_username = 'username';
  62 
  63 /**
  64  * Password for the specified user name.
  65  *
  66  * The default password is empty.
  67  *
  68  * @global string $g_db_password
  69  */
  70 $g_db_password = 'passwprd';
  71 
  72 /**
  73  * Name of database that contains MantisBT tables.
  74  *
  75  * The default database name is "bugtracker".
  76  *
  77  * @global string $g_database_name
  78  */
  79 $g_database_name = 'bugtracker';
  80 
  81 /**
  82  * Defines the database type.
  83  *
  84  * Supported types are listed below; the corresponding PHP extension must be enabled.
  85  *
  86  * RDBMS           db_type       PHP ext   Comments
  87  * -----           -------       -------   --------
  88  * MySQL           mysqli        mysqli    default
  89  * PostgreSQL      pgsql         pgsql
  90  * MS SQL Server   mssqlnative   sqlsrv    experimental
  91  * Oracle          oci8          oci8      experimental
  92  *
  93  * @global string $g_db_type
  94  */
  95 $g_db_type = 'mysqli';
  96 
  97 /**
  98  * Adodb Data Source Name.
  99  *
 100  * This is an EXPERIMENTAL field.
 101  *
 102  * If the above database settings, do not provide enough flexibility, it is
 103  * possible to specify a dsn for the database connection. For further details,
 104  * currently, you need to see the adodb manual at
 105  * http://phplens.com/adodb/code.initialization.html#dsnsupport. For example,
 106  * if db_type is odbc_mssql. The following is an example dsn:
 107  * "Driver={SQL Server Native Client 10.0};SERVER=.\sqlexpress;DATABASE=bugtracker;UID=mantis;PWD=password;"
 108  *
 109  * NOTE: the installer does not yet fully support the use of dsn's
 110  *
 111  * @global string $g_dsn
 112  */
 113 $g_dsn = '';
 114 
 115 /**
 116  * Database Table prefix.
 117  *
 118  * The given string is added with an underscore before the base table name,
 119  * e.g. 'bug' => 'mantis_bug'.
 120  * To avoid the 30-char limit on identifiers in Oracle (< 12cR2), the prefix
 121  * should be set to blank or kept as short as possible (e.g. 'm')
 122  *
 123  * @global string $g_db_table_prefix
 124  */
 125 $g_db_table_prefix = 'mantis';
 126 
 127 /**
 128  * Database Table suffix.
 129  *
 130  * The given string is added with an underscore after the base table name,
 131  * e.g. 'bug' => 'bug_table'.
 132  * To avoid the 30-char limit on identifiers in Oracle (< 12cR2), the prefix
 133  * should be set to blank or kept as short as possible.
 134  * @see $g_db_table_prefix for size limitation recommendation
 135  *
 136  * @global string $g_db_table_suffix
 137  */
 138 $g_db_table_suffix = '_table';
 139 
 140 /**
 141  * Plugin Table prefix.
 142  *
 143  * The given string is added with an underscore between the table prefix and
 144  * the base table name, and the plugin basename is added after that
 145  * e.g. 'Example' plugin's table 'foo' => 'mantis_plugin_Example_foo_table'.
 146  * To avoid the 30-char limit on identifiers in Oracle (< 12cR2), the prefix
 147  * should be kept as short as possible (e.g. 'plg').
 148  * It is strongly recommended not to use an empty string here.
 149  *
 150  * @see $g_db_table_prefix
 151  * @global string $g_db_table_plugin_prefix
 152  */
 153 $g_db_table_plugin_prefix = 'plugin';

 157 ####################

 159 /**
 160  * Path to root MantisBT folder.
 161  *
 162  * Requires trailing / or \.
 163  *
 164  * @global string $g_absolute_path
 165  */
 166 $g_absolute_path = __DIR__ . DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR;
 167 
 168 /**
 169  * Path to core folder.

 171  * The default is usually OK, unless you moved the 'core' directory out of your
 172  * webroot (recommended).

 175  */

 187 /**

 191  *

 313 #############################
 314 # Security and Cryptography #
 315 #############################
 316 
 317 /**
 318  * Master salt value used for cryptographic hashing throughout MantisBT.
 319  *
 320  * This value must be kept secret at all costs. You must generate a unique and
 321  * random salt value for each installation of MantisBT you control. The
 322  * minimum length of this string must be at least 16 characters.
 323  *
 324  * The value you select for this salt should be a long string generated using
 325  * a secure random number generator. An example for Linux systems is:
 326  *
 327  *    cat /dev/urandom | head -c 64 | base64
 328  *
 329  * Note that the number of bits of entropy per byte of output from /dev/urandom
 330  * is not 8. If you're particularly paranoid and don't mind waiting a long
 331  * time, you could use /dev/random to get much closer to 8 bits of entropy per
 332  * byte. Moving the mouse (if possible) while generating entropy via
 333  * /dev/random will greatly improve the speed at which /dev/random produces
 334  * entropy.
 335  *
 336  * WARNING: This configuration option has a profound impact on the security of
 337  * your MantisBT installation. Failure to set this configuration option
 338  * correctly could lead to your MantisBT installation being compromised. Ensure
 339  * that this value remains secret. Treat it with the same security that you'd
 340  * treat the password to your MantisDB database.
 341  *
 342  * This setting is blank by default. MantisBT will not operate in this state.
 343  * Hence, you are forced to change the value of this configuration option.
 344  *
 345  * @global string $g_crypto_master_salt
 346  */
 347 $g_crypto_master_salt = '';
 348

 549 /**
 550  * Sets notifications overrides for specific actions/statuses.
 551  *
 552  * If a user category is not listed for an action, the default defined by
 553  * {@see $g_default_notify_flags} is used.
 554  *
 555  * Possible actions are:
 556  * - `new`:      a new Issue has been added
 557  * - `owner`:    an Issue has been assigned to a new owner
 558  * - `reopened`: an Issue has been reopened
 559  * - `deleted`:  an Issue has been deleted
 560  * - `updated`:  an Issue has been updated
 561  * - `bugnote`:  a bugnote has been added to an Issue
 562  * - `sponsor`:  sponsorship has changed on this Issue
 563  * - `relation`: a relationship has changed on this Issue
 564  * - `monitor`:  an Issue is monitored.
 565  * - `<status>`: A status code, as defined in {@see $g_status_enum_string},
 566  *               eg: 'resolved', 'closed', 'feedback', 'acknowledged`, etc.
 567  *
 568  * Examples:
 569  *  - If you wanted to have all developers get notified of new bugs you could
 570  *    add the following lines to your config file:
 571  *
 572  *    $g_notify_flags['new']['threshold_min'] = DEVELOPER;
 573  *    $g_notify_flags['new']['threshold_max'] = DEVELOPER;
 574  *
 575  *  - You might want to do something similar so all managers are notified when a
 576  *    bug is closed.
 577  *  - If you did not want reporters to be notified when a bug is closed
 578  *    (only when it is resolved) you would use:
 579  *
 580  *    $g_notify_flags['closed']['reporter'] = OFF;
 581  *
 582  * The default setting
 583  * - disables bugnotes notifications on new bugs (not needed in this case)
 584  * - disables all notifications for the monitoring event, except explicit
 585  *

 587  * @global array $g_notify_flags
 588  */

 933 /**

 935  *
 936  * When this is ON (recommended), instead of sending of emails as soon as an
 937  * action is performed (typically at the end of each page), emails are queued
 938  * and must be sent manually by executing 'scripts/send_emails.php'. This script
 939  * can only be run from the CLI, not from the web interface, for security reasons.
 940  * The script's execution is typically handled by a cron job or a scheduler task,
 941  * set to run every few minutes.
 942  *
 943  * If no cronjob is used (default), then the user will have to wait for MantisBT
 944  * to process the email queue after each page load.

 947  */

2381 ##########################
2382 # MantisBT HTML Settings #

2385 /**
2386  * Convert URLs and e-mail addresses to html links.
2387  *
2388  * This flag controls whether URLs and email addresses are automatically
2389  * converted to clickable links. Additionally, for URL links, it determines
2390  * where they open when clicked (*target* attribute) and their type.
2391  *
2392  * The options below can be combined using bitwise operators (not all
2393  * possible combinations make sense):
2394  * - OFF                      Do not convert URLs or emails
2395  * - LINKS_SAME_WINDOW        Convert to links that open in the current window (DEFAULT)
2396  * - LINKS_NEW_WINDOW         Convert to links that open in a new window (overrides LINKS_SAME_WINDOW)
2397  * - LINKS_NOOPENER           Links have the `noopener` type (DEFAULT)
2398  *                            {@link https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/rel/noopener}
2399  * - LINKS_NOREFERRER         Links have the `noreferrer` type, i.e. they omit the *Referer*
2400  *                            header (implies LINKS_NOOPENER)
2401  *                            {@link https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/rel/noreferrer}
2402  * - LINKS_NOFOLLOW_EXTERNAL  Links to external sites (i.e. having a different root domain)
2403  *                            have the `nofollow` type, instructing search engines
2404  *                            not to follow these links (DEFAULT)
2405  *                            {@link https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/rel#nofollow}
2406  *
2407  * @global int $g_html_make_links
2408  */
2409 $g_html_make_links = LINKS_SAME_WINDOW | LINKS_NOOPENER | LINKS_NOFOLLOW_EXTERNAL;
2410

2417  *
2418  * @global string $g_html_valid_tags
2419  */

2421 
2422 /**
2423  * Valid html tags for single line fields (e.g. issue summary).

2427  *  - tags that require attributes

2430  */
2431 $g_html_valid_tags_single_line = 'i, b, u, em, strong';

2498 /**
2499  * Specifies the LDAP or Active Directory server(s) to connect to.
2500  *
2501  * This must be a full LDAP URI (ldap[s]://hostname:port)
2502  * - Protocol must be either:
2503  *   - ldap - unencrypted or opportunistic TLS (STARTTLS) {@see $g_ldap_use_starttls}
2504  *   - ldaps - for TLS encryption
2505  * - Port number is optional, and defaults to 389. If this doesn't work, try
2506  *   using one of the following standard port numbers: 636 (ldaps); for Active
2507  *   Directory Global Catalog forest-wide search, use 3268 (ldap) or 3269 (ldaps)
2508  *
2509  * Examples of valid URI:
2510  *   ldap://ldap.example.com
2511  *   ldaps://ldap.example.com:3269/
2512  *
2513  * Multiple servers can be specified as a space-separated list.
2514  *
2515  * @global string $g_ldap_server
2516  */
2517 $g_ldap_server = 'ldap://ldap.example.com/';
2518 
2519 /**
2520  * Determines whether the connection will attempt an opportunistic upgrade
2521  * to a TLS connection (STARTTLS).
2522  *
2523  * For security, a failure aborts the entire connection, so make sure your
2524  * server supports StartTLS if this setting is ON, and use the ldap:// scheme
2525  * (not ldaps://).
2526  *
2527  * @global int $g_ldap_use_starttls
2528  */
2529 $g_ldap_use_starttls = ON;
2530 
2531 /**
2532  * The minimum version of the TLS protocol to allow.
2533  *
2534  * This maps to the LDAP_OPT_X_TLS_PROTOCOL_MIN ldap library option.
2535  * For example, LDAP_OPT_X_TLS_PROTOCOL_TLS1_2. If OFF (default), then the
2536  * protocol version is not set.
2537  *
2538  * Requires PHP 7.1 or later.
2539  * For security, a failure aborts the entire connection.
2540  *
2541  * @see https://www.php.net/manual/en/ldap.constants.php#constant.ldap-opt-x-tls-protocol-min
2542  *
2543  * @global int $g_ldap_tls_protocol_min
2544  */
2545 $g_ldap_tls_protocol_min = OFF;
2546 
2547 /**
2548  * The root distinguished name for LDAP searches.
2549  *
2550  * @global string $g_ldap_root_dn
2551  */
2552 $g_ldap_root_dn = 'dc=example,dc=com';
2553 
2554 /**
2555  * LDAP search filter for the organization.
2556  *
2557  * e.g. '(organizationname=*Traffic)'
2558  *
2559  * @global string $g_ldap_organization
2560  */
2561 $g_ldap_organization = '';
2562 
2563 /**
2564  * The LDAP Protocol Version.
2565  *
2566  * This maps to the LDAP_OPT_PROTOCOL_VERSION ldap library option.
2567  *
2568  * Possible values are 2, 3 (default) or 0. If 0, then the protocol version is
2569  * not set, and you get whatever default the underlying ldap library uses.
2570  * In almost all cases you should use 3. LDAPv3 was introduced back in 1997.
2571  * LDAPv2 was deprecated in 2003 by RFC3494.
2572  *
2573  * @global int $g_ldap_protocol_version
2574  */
2575 $g_ldap_protocol_version = 3;
2576 
2577 /**
2578  * Duration of the timeout for TCP connection to the LDAP server (in seconds).
2579  *
2580  * This maps to the LDAP_OPT_NETWORK_TIMEOUT ldap library option.
2581  *
2582  * Set this to a low value when the hostname defined in $g_ldap_server resolves
2583  * to multiple IP addresses, allowing rapid failover to the next available LDAP
2584  * server.
2585  * Defaults to 0 (infinite).
2586  *
2587  * @global int $g_ldap_network_timeout
2588  */
2589 $g_ldap_network_timeout = 0;
2590 
2591 /**
2592  * Determines whether the LDAP library automatically follows referrals returned
2593  * by LDAP servers or not.
2594  *
2595  * This maps to the LDAP_OPT_REFERRALS ldap library option.
2596  *
2597  * For Active Directory, this should be set to OFF.
2598  * If you have only one LDAP server, setting to this to OFF is advisable to prevent
2599  * any man-in-the-middle attacks.
2600  *
2601  * @global int $g_ldap_follow_referrals
2602  */
2603 $g_ldap_follow_referrals = ON;
2604 
2605 /**
2606  * The distinguished name of the service account to use for binding to the
2607  * LDAP server.
2608  *
2609  * For anonymous binding, leave empty.
2610  * For example, 'cn=ldap,ou=Administrators,dc=example,dc=com'.
2611  *
2612  * @global string $g_ldap_bind_dn
2613  */
2614 $g_ldap_bind_dn = '';
2615 
2616 /**
2617  * The password for the service account used to establish the connection to
2618  * the LDAP server.
2619  *
2620  * For anonymous binding, leave empty.
2621  *
2622  * @global string $g_ldap_bind_passwd
2623  */
2624 $g_ldap_bind_passwd = '';
2625 
2626 /**
2627  * The LDAP field for username.
2628  *
2629  * Use 'sAMAccountName' for Active Directory.
2630  *
2631  * @global string $g_ldap_uid_field
2632  */
2633 $g_ldap_uid_field = 'uid';
2634 
2635 /**
2636  * The LDAP field for the user's e-mail address.
2637  *
2638  * @see $g_use_ldap_email
2639  * @global string $g_ldap_email_field
2640  */
2641 $g_ldap_email_field = 'mail';
2642 
2643 /**
2644  * The LDAP field for the user's real name (i.e. common name).
2645  *
2646  * @see $g_use_ldap_realname
2647  * @global string $g_ldap_realname_field
2648  */
2649 $g_ldap_realname_field = 'cn';
2650 
2651 /**
2652  * Use the realname specified in LDAP (ON) rather than the one stored in the
2653  * database (OFF).
2654  *
2655  * Note that MantisBT will update the database with the data retrieved

2663 /**

2667  * Note that MantisBT will update the database with the data retrieved

2669  *

2675 /**
2676  * LDAP server simulation.

2678  * This configuration option allows replacing the LDAP server with a comma-

2680  *
2681  * The LDAP simulation file format is as follows:

3832 /**
3833  * Protection against CSV Injection.
3834  *
3835  * When this setting is ON (default), any data that could be interpreted as a
3836  * formula by a spreadsheet program such as Excel (i.e. starting with `=`, `@`,
3837  * `-` or `+`), will be prefixed with a tab character (\t) in order to prevent
3838  * CSV injection.
3839  *
3840  * Sometimes this may not be appropriate (e.g. if the CSV needs to be consumed
3841  * programmatically). In that case, $g_csv_injection_protection can be set to OFF,
3842  * resulting in raw data to be exported.
3843  *
3844  * Setting this to OFF is a security risk. An attacker could upload a crafted
3845  * CSV file containing formulas that will be executed when opened with Excel,
3846  * as described in this article {@link http://georgemauer.net/2017/10/07/csv-injection.html}.
3847  *
3848  * @global string $g_csv_injection_protection
3849  */
3850 $g_csv_injection_protection = ON;

4679  * details.

4682  *

4695  *	array(
4696  *		'action' => 'EXT_ADD_NOTE',  # you need to implement bug_actiongroup_<action_without_'EXT_')_inc.php
4697  *		'label' => 'actiongroup_menu_add_note' # see strings_english.txt for this label
4698  *	)
4699  * );

4996 /**
4997  * Default due date value for newly submitted issues.
4998  *
4999  * A valid relative date format {@link https://php.net/manual/en/datetime.formats.relative.php}
5000  * e.g. 'today' or '+2 days', or empty string for no due date set (default).
5001  *
5002  * @global string $g_due_date_default
5003  */
5004 $g_due_date_default = '';
5005 
5006 /**
5007  * Due date warning levels.
5008  *
5009  * A variable number of Levels (defined as a number of seconds going backwards
5010  * from the current timestamp, compared to an issue's due date) can be defined.
5011  * Levels must be defined in ascending order.
5012  *
5013  * - The first entry (array key 0) defines "Overdue". Normally and by default,
5014  *   its value is `0` meaning that issues will be marked overdue as soon as
5015  *   their due date has passed. However, it is also possible to set it to a
5016  *   higher value to flag overdue issues earlier, or even use a negative value
5017  *   to allow a "grace period" after due date.
5018  * - Array keys 1 and 2 offer two levels of "Due soon": orange and green.
5019  *   By default, only the first one is set, to 7 days.
5020  *
5021  * Out of the box, MantisBT allows for 3 warning levels. Additional ones may
5022  * be defined, but in that case new `due-N` CSS rules (where N is the
5023  * array's index) must be created otherwise the extra levels will not be
5024  * highlighted in the UI.
5025  *
5026  * @global  array $g_due_date_warning_levels
5027  */
5028 $g_due_date_warning_levels = array(
5029 	0,
5030 	7 * SECONDS_PER_DAY,
5031 );

5101  */
5102 $g_show_queries_count = OFF;
5103 
5104 /**
5105  * Errors Display method.
5106  *
5107  * Defines what {@link http://php.net/errorfunc.constants errors}
5108  * are displayed and how. Available options are:
5109  * - DISPLAY_ERROR_HALT    Stop and display error message (including
5110  *                         variables and backtrace if
5111  *                         {@see $g_show_detailed_errors} is ON).
5112  * - DISPLAY_ERROR_INLINE  Display a one line error and continue execution.
5113  * - DISPLAY_ERROR_NONE    Suppress the error (no display). This is the default
5114  *                         behavior for unspecified errors constants.
5115  *
5116  * The default settings are recommended for use in Production, and will only
5117  * display MantisBT fatal errors, suppressing output of all other error types.
5118  *
5119  * Recommended config_inc.php settings for developers (these are automatically
5120  * set if the server is localhost):
5121  * $g_display_errors = array(
5122  *     E_WARNING           => DISPLAY_ERROR_HALT,
5123  *     E_ALL               => DISPLAY_ERROR_INLINE,
5124  * );
5125  *
5126  * NOTE: E_USER_ERROR, E_RECOVERABLE_ERROR and E_ERROR will always be set
5127  * to DISPLAY_ERROR_HALT internally, regardless of the configured value.
5128  *
5129  * @global array $g_display_errors
5130  */
5131 $g_display_errors = array();
5132 
5133 # Add developers defaults when server is localhost
5134 # Note: intentionally not using SERVER_ADDR as it's not guaranteed to exist
5135 if( isset( $_SERVER['SERVER_NAME'] ) &&
5136 	( strcasecmp( $_SERVER['SERVER_NAME'], 'localhost' ) == 0 ||
5137 	  $_SERVER['SERVER_NAME'] == '127.0.0.1' )
5138 ) {
5139 	$g_display_errors[E_WARNING] = DISPLAY_ERROR_HALT;
5140 	$g_display_errors[E_ALL] = DISPLAY_ERROR_INLINE;
5141 }
5142 
5143 /**
5144  * Detailed error messages.
5145  *
5146  * Shows a list of variables and their values, as well as an execution stack
5147  * trace whenever a fatal error is triggered.
5148  *
5149  * Only applies to error types configured to DISPLAY_ERROR_HALT in
5150  * {@see $g_display_errors}.
5151  *
5152  * WARNING: Setting this to ON is a potential security hazard, as it can expose
5153  * sensitive system information. Only enable it when needed for debugging purposes.
5154  *
5155  * @global int $g_show_detailed_errors
5156  */
5157 $g_show_detailed_errors = OFF;
5158 
5159 /**
5160  * Prevent page redirections when non-fatal errors occur.
5161  *
5162  * If this option is turned OFF (default) page redirects will function normally,
5163  * preventing display of non-fatal error messages.
5164  *
5165  * It should only be set to ON during development or for debugging purposes.
5166  * This will prevent page redirections, allowing you to see the errors.
5167  *
5168  * NOTE: Non-fatal errors are those configured as DISPLAY_ERROR_INLINE in
5169  * {@see $g_display_errors}.
5170  *
5171  * @global int $g_stop_on_errors
5172  */
5173 $g_stop_on_errors = OFF;
5174 
5175 /**
5176  * System logging.
5177  *
5178  * This controls the type of logging information recorded.
5179  * The available log channels are:
5180  *
5181  * LOG_NONE, LOG_EMAIL, LOG_EMAIL_RECIPIENT, LOG_EMAIL_VERBOSE, LOG_FILTERING,
5182  * LOG_AJAX, LOG_LDAP, LOG_DATABASE, LOG_WEBSERVICE, LOG_PLUGIN, LOG_ALL
5183  *
5184  * and can be combined using
5185  * {@link http://php.net/language.operators.bitwise PHP bitwise operators}
5186  * Refer to {@see $g_log_destination} for details on where to save the logs.
5187  *
5188  * @global int $g_log_level
5189  */
5190 $g_log_level = LOG_NONE;
5191 
5192 /**
5193  * Specifies where the log data goes.
5194  *
5195  * The following five options are available:
5196  * - '':        The empty string means {@link http://php.net/error_log
5197  *              default PHP error log settings}
5198  * - 'none':    Don't output the logs, but would still trigger EVENT_LOG
5199  *              plugin event.
5200  * - 'file':    Log to a specific file, specified as an absolute path, e.g.
5201  *              'file:/var/log/mantis.log' (Unix) or
5202  *              'file:c:/temp/mantisbt.log' (Windows)
5203  * - 'page':    Display log output at bottom of the page. See also
5204  *              {@link $g_show_log_threshold} to restrict who can see log data.
5205  *
5206  * @global string $g_log_destination
5207  */
5208 $g_log_destination = '';
5209 
5210 /**
5211  * Indicates the access level required for a user to see the log output.

5216  * rather than the one from the currently active project.
5217  *
5218  * @global int $g_show_log_threshold
5219  */
5220 $g_show_log_threshold = ADMINISTRATOR;

  17 /**
  18  * MantisBT Core
  19  *
  20  * Initialises the MantisBT core, connects to the database, starts plugins and
  21  * performs other global operations that either help initialise MantisBT or
  22  * are required to be executed on every page load.
  23  *
  24  * @package MantisBT

  26  * @copyright Copyright 2002  MantisBT Team - mantisbt-dev@lists.sourceforge.net
  27  * @link http://www.mantisbt.org

  29  * @uses authentication_api.php
  30  * @uses collapse_api.php
  31  * @uses compress_api.php
  32  * @uses config_api.php
  33  * @uses config_defaults_inc.php
  34  * @uses config_inc.php
  35  * @uses constant_inc.php
  36  * @uses crypto_api.php
  37  * @uses custom_constants_inc.php
  38  * @uses custom_functions_inc.php
  39  * @uses database_api.php
  40  * @uses event_api.php
  41  * @uses http_api.php
  42  * @uses lang_api.php
  43  * @uses mantis_offline.php
  44  * @uses plugin_api.php
  45  * @uses php_api.php
  46  * @uses user_pref_api.php
  47  * @uses wiki_api.php
  48  *
  49  * @noinspection PhpIncludeInspection
  50  */
  51 
  52 /**
  53  * Before doing anything... check if MantisBT is down for maintenance
  54  *
  55  *   To make MantisBT 'offline' simply create a file called
  56  *   'mantis_offline.php' in the MantisBT root directory.
  57  *   Users are redirected to that file if it exists.
  58  *   If you have to test MantisBT while it's offline, add the
  59  *   parameter 'mbadmin=1' to the URL.
  60  */
  61 if( file_exists( 'mantis_offline.php' ) && !isset( $_GET['mbadmin'] ) ) {
  62 	include( 'mantis_offline.php' );
  63 	exit;
  64 }
  65 
  66 $g_request_time = microtime( true );
  67 
  68 # Load supplied constants
  69 require_once( __DIR__ . '/core/constant_inc.php' );
  70 
  71 # Enforce our minimum PHP requirements
  72 if( version_compare( PHP_VERSION, PHP_MIN_VERSION, '<' ) ) {
  73 	$C = 'constant';
  74 	die( <<<MESSAGE
  75 		<h2>FATAL ERROR: Your version of PHP is too old</h2>
  76 		<p>MantisBT {$C('MANTIS_VERSION')} requires PHP {$C('PHP_MIN_VERSION')} or newer.</p>
  77 		You are running version <em>{$C('PHP_VERSION')}</em>.
  78 		Please upgrade to a newer version.
  79 		MESSAGE
  80 	);
  81 }
  82 if( defined( 'PHP_MAX_VERSION' )
  83 	&& version_compare( PHP_VERSION, PHP_MAX_VERSION, '>=' )
  84 ) {
  85 	# URL to filter by PHP version tag
  86 	preg_match( '/\d+\.\d+/', PHP_MAX_VERSION, $t_short_version );
  87 	$t_mantis_url = 'https://mantisbt.org/bugs/search.php?project_id=1&tag_string=PHP%20' . $t_short_version[0];
  88 
  89 	$C = 'constant';
  90 	die(<<<MESSAGE
  91 		<h2>FATAL ERROR: MantisBT {$C('MANTIS_VERSION')} has known issues with PHP {$C('PHP_MAX_VERSION')} or later</strong></h2>
  92 		<p>Please refer to the <a href='$t_mantis_url'>bug tracker</a> for details.</p>
  93 		You are running PHP <em>{$C('PHP_VERSION')}</em>. 
  94 		Please downgrade to an earlier version.
  95 		MESSAGE
  96 	);
  97 }
  98 
  99 ensure_php_extension_loaded( 'mbstring', 'for Unicode (UTF-8) support' );
 100 
 101 # Ensure that encoding is always UTF-8 independent from any PHP default or ini setting
 102 mb_internal_encoding( 'UTF-8' );
 103 
 104 if( php_sapi_name() != 'cli' ) {
 105 	ob_start();
 106 }
 107 
 108 # Load Composer autoloader
 109 require_once( __DIR__ . '/vendor/autoload.php' );
 110 
 111 # Include default configuration settings
 112 require_once( __DIR__ . '/config_defaults_inc.php' );
 113 
 114 # Load user-defined constants (if required)
 115 global $g_config_path;
 116 if( file_exists( $g_config_path . 'custom_constants_inc.php' ) ) {
 117 	require_once( $g_config_path . 'custom_constants_inc.php' );
 118 }
 119 
 120 # config_inc may not be present if this is a new install
 121 $t_config_inc_found = file_exists( $g_config_path . 'config_inc.php' );
 122 if( $t_config_inc_found ) {
 123 	require_once( $g_config_path . 'config_inc.php' );
 124 }
 125 
 126 # Set global path variables
 127 # NOTE: We store whether $g_path was defaulted, so we can later warn the admin
 128 # about the exposure to host header injection attacks if they didn't set it.
 129 global $g_defaulted_path;
 130 $g_defaulted_path = set_default_path();
 131 
 132 # Ensure PHP LDAP extension is available when Login Method is LDAP
 133 global $g_login_method;
 134 if ( $g_login_method == LDAP ) {
 135 	ensure_php_extension_loaded( 'ldap', 'when using LDAP as Login Method' );
 136 }
 137 
 138 # Register the autoload function to make it effective immediately
 139 spl_autoload_register( 'autoload_mantis' );
 140 
 141 # Include PHP compatibility file
 142 require_api( 'php_api.php' );
 143 
 144 # Ensure that output is blank so far (output at this stage generally denotes
 145 # that an error has occurred)
 146 if( ( $t_output = ob_get_contents() ) != '' ) {
 147 	echo 'Possible Whitespace/Error in Configuration File - Aborting. Output so far follows:<br />';
 148 	var_dump( $t_output );
 149 	die;
 150 }
 151 unset( $t_output );
 152 
 153 # Start HTML compression handler (if enabled)
 154 require_api( 'compress_api.php' );
 155 compress_start_handler();
 156 
 157 # If no configuration file exists, redirect the user to the admin page so
 158 # they can complete installation and configuration of MantisBT
 159 if( false === $t_config_inc_found ) {
 160 	if( php_sapi_name() == 'cli' ) {
 161 		echo 'Error: ' . $g_config_path . "config_inc.php file not found; ensure MantisBT is properly setup.\n";
 162 		exit( 1 );
 163 	}
 164 
 165 	# Do not load Core for dynamic javascript files when MantisBT is not installed
 166 	if( isset( $_SERVER['SCRIPT_NAME'] ) && ( 0 < strpos( $_SERVER['SCRIPT_NAME'], 'javascript' ) ) ) {
 167 		http_response_code( HTTP_STATUS_NO_CONTENT );
 168 		exit;
 169 	}
 170 
 171 	if( !( isset( $_SERVER['SCRIPT_NAME'] ) && ( 0 < strpos( $_SERVER['SCRIPT_NAME'], 'admin' ) ) ) ) {
 172 		header( 'Content-Type: text/html' );
 173 		# Temporary redirect (307) instead of Found (302) default
 174 		header( 'Location: admin/install.php', true, 307 );
 175 		# Make sure it's not cached
 176 		header( 'Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate' );
 177 		exit;
 178 	}
 179 }
 180 
 181 # Initialise cryptographic keys
 182 require_api( 'crypto_api.php' );
 183 crypto_init();
 184 
 185 # Connect to the database
 186 require_api( 'database_api.php' );
 187 require_api( 'config_api.php' );
 188 
 189 # Set the default timezone
 190 # To reduce overhead, we assume that the timezone configuration is valid,
 191 # i.e. it exists in timezone_identifiers_list(). If not, a PHP NOTICE will
 192 # be raised and we fall back to the system's default timezone.
 193 # Use admin checks to validate configuration.
 194 $t_tz = config_get_global( 'default_timezone' );
 195 if( empty( $t_tz ) || !date_default_timezone_set( $t_tz ) ) {
 196 	$t_tz = date_default_timezone_get();
 197 }
 198 config_set_global( 'default_timezone', $t_tz );
 199 
 200 if( !defined( 'MANTIS_MAINTENANCE_MODE' ) ) {
 201 	global $g_use_persistent_connections, $g_hostname, $g_db_username, $g_db_password, $g_database_name;
 202 	if( OFF == $g_use_persistent_connections ) {
 203 		db_connect( config_get_global( 'dsn', false ), $g_hostname, $g_db_username, $g_db_password, $g_database_name );
 204 	} else {
 205 		db_connect( config_get_global( 'dsn', false ), $g_hostname, $g_db_username, $g_db_password, $g_database_name, true );
 206 	}
 207 }
 208 
 209 # Register global shutdown function
 210 shutdown_functions_register();
 211 
 212 # Push default language to speed calls to lang_get
 213 if( !defined( 'LANG_LOAD_DISABLED' ) ) {
 214 	require_api( 'lang_api.php' );
 215 	lang_push( lang_get_default() );
 216 }
 217 
 218 # Initialise plugins
 219 require_api( 'plugin_api.php' );  # necessary for some upgrade steps
 220 if( !defined( 'PLUGINS_DISABLED' ) && !defined( 'MANTIS_MAINTENANCE_MODE' ) ) {
 221 	plugin_init_installed();
 222 }
 223 
 224 # Initialise Wiki integration
 225 if( config_get_global( 'wiki_enable' ) == ON ) {
 226 	require_api( 'wiki_api.php' );
 227 	wiki_init();
 228 }
 229 
 230 if( !isset( $g_login_anonymous ) ) {
 231 	$g_login_anonymous = true;
 232 }
 233 
 234 if( !defined( 'MANTIS_MAINTENANCE_MODE' ) ) {
 235 	require_api( 'authentication_api.php' );
 236 
 237 	# Override the default timezone according to user's preferences
 238 	if( auth_is_user_authenticated() ) {
 239 		require_api( 'user_pref_api.php' );
 240 		$t_tz = user_pref_get_pref( auth_get_current_user_id(), 'timezone' );
 241 		@date_default_timezone_set( $t_tz );
 242 	}
 243 }
 244 unset( $t_tz );
 245 
 246 # Cache current user's collapse API data
 247 if( !defined( 'MANTIS_MAINTENANCE_MODE' ) ) {
 248 	require_api( 'collapse_api.php' );
 249 	collapse_cache_token();
 250 }
 251 
 252 # Load custom functions
 253 require_api( 'custom_function_api.php' );
 254 
 255 if( file_exists( $g_config_path . 'custom_functions_inc.php' ) ) {
 256 	require_once( $g_config_path . 'custom_functions_inc.php' );
 257 }
 258 
 259 # Set HTTP response headers
 260 require_api( 'http_api.php' );
 261 event_signal( 'EVENT_CORE_HEADERS' );
 262 http_all_headers();
 263 
 264 # Signal plugins that the core system is loaded
 265 if( !defined( 'PLUGINS_DISABLED' ) && !defined( 'MANTIS_MAINTENANCE_MODE' ) ) {
 266 	require_api( 'event_api.php' );
 267 	event_signal( 'EVENT_CORE_READY' );
 268 }

 270 /**
 271  * Define an API inclusion function to replace require_once
 272  *
 273  * @param string $p_api_name An API file name.
 274  * @return void
 275  */
 276 function require_api( $p_api_name ) {
 277 	static $s_api_included;
 278 	global $g_core_path;
 279 	if( !isset( $s_api_included[$p_api_name] ) ) {
 280 		require_once( $g_core_path . $p_api_name );
 281 		$t_new_globals = array_diff_key( get_defined_vars(), $GLOBALS, array( 't_new_globals' => 0 ) );
 282 		foreach ( $t_new_globals as $t_global_name => $t_global_value ) {
 283 			$GLOBALS[$t_global_name] = $t_global_value;
 284 		}
 285 		$s_api_included[$p_api_name] = 1;
 286 	}
 287 }
 288 
 289 /**
 290  * Define an API inclusion function to replace require_once
 291  *
 292  * @param string $p_library_name A library file name.
 293  * @return void
 294  */
 295 function require_lib( $p_library_name ) {
 296 	static $s_libraries_included;
 297 
 298 	if( !isset( $s_libraries_included[$p_library_name] ) ) {
 299 		global $g_library_path;
 300 		$t_library_file_path = $g_library_path . $p_library_name;
 301 
 302 		if( file_exists( $t_library_file_path ) ) {
 303 			require_once( $t_library_file_path );
 304 		} else {
 305 			echo 'External library \'' . $t_library_file_path . '\' not found.';
 306 			exit;
 307 		}
 308 
 309 		$t_new_globals = array_diff_key( get_defined_vars(), $GLOBALS, array( 't_new_globals' => 0 ) );
 310 		foreach ( $t_new_globals as $t_global_name => $t_global_value ) {
 311 			$GLOBALS[$t_global_name] = $t_global_value;
 312 		}
 313 
 314 		$s_libraries_included[$p_library_name] = 1;
 315 	}
 316 }
 317 
 318 /**
 319  * Checks to see if script was queried through the HTTPS protocol
 320  * @return boolean True if protocol is HTTPS
 321  */
 322 function http_is_protocol_https() {
 323 	if( isset( $_SERVER['HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PROTO'] ) ) {
 324 		return strtolower( $_SERVER['HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PROTO'] ) == 'https';
 325 	}
 326 
 327 	if( !empty( $_SERVER['HTTPS'] ) && ( strtolower( $_SERVER['HTTPS'] ) != 'off' ) ) {
 328 		return true;
 329 	}
 330 
 331 	return false;
 332 }
 333 
 334 /**
 335  * Set Global Path variables.
 336  *
 337  * @see $g_path
 338  * @see $g_short_path
 339  *
 340  * @return bool True if default $g_path was assigned, false if it was already set.
 341  */
 342 function set_default_path() {
 343 	global $g_path, $g_short_path, $g_config_path;
 344 
 345 	# $g_path is set in config_inc.php
 346 	if( $g_path ) {
 347 		# Derive $g_short_path from $g_path if not set
 348 		if( !$g_short_path ) {
 349 			$g_short_path = parse_url( $g_path, PHP_URL_PATH );
 350 		}
 351 		return false;
 352 	}
 353 
 354 	$t_protocol = 'http';
 355 	$t_host = 'localhost';
 356 	if( isset( $_SERVER['SCRIPT_NAME'] ) ) {
 357 		$t_protocol = http_is_protocol_https() ? 'https' : 'http';
 358 
 359 		# $_SERVER['SERVER_PORT'] is not defined in case of php-cgi.exe
 360 		if( isset( $_SERVER['SERVER_PORT'] ) ) {
 361 			$t_port = ':' . $_SERVER['SERVER_PORT'];
 362 			if( ( ':80' == $t_port && 'http' == $t_protocol )
 363 				|| ( ':443' == $t_port && 'https' == $t_protocol )) {
 364 				$t_port = '';
 365 			}
 366 		} else {
 367 			$t_port = '';
 368 		}
 369 
 370 		if( isset( $_SERVER['HTTP_X_FORWARDED_HOST'] ) ) { # Support ProxyPass
 371 			$t_hosts = explode( ',', $_SERVER['HTTP_X_FORWARDED_HOST'] );
 372 			$t_host = $t_hosts[0];
 373 		} else if( isset( $_SERVER['HTTP_HOST'] ) ) {
 374 			$t_host = $_SERVER['HTTP_HOST'];
 375 		} else if( isset( $_SERVER['SERVER_NAME'] ) ) {
 376 			$t_host = $_SERVER['SERVER_NAME'] . $t_port;
 377 		} else if( isset( $_SERVER['SERVER_ADDR'] ) ) {
 378 			$t_host = $_SERVER['SERVER_ADDR'] . $t_port;
 379 		}
 380 
 381 		# Prevent XSS if the path is displayed later on. This is the equivalent of
 382 		# FILTER_SANITIZE_STRING, which was deprecated in PHP 8.1:
 383 		# strip tags and null bytes, then encode quotes into HTML entities
 384 		$t_path = preg_replace( '/\x00|<[^>]*>?/', '', $_SERVER['SCRIPT_NAME'] );
 385 		$t_path = str_replace( ["'", '"'], ['&#39;', '&#34;'], $t_path );
 386 
 387 		$t_path = dirname( $t_path );
 388 		switch( basename( $t_path ) ) {
 389 			case 'admin':
 390 				$t_path = dirname( $t_path );
 391 				break;
 392 			case 'check': # admin checks dir
 393 			case 'soap':
 394 			case 'rest':
 395 				$t_path = dirname( $t_path, 2 );
 396 				break;
 397 			case 'swagger':
 398 				$t_path = dirname( $t_path, 3 );
 399 				break;
 400 		}
 401 		$t_path = rtrim( $t_path, '/\\' ) . '/';
 402 
 403 		if( strpos( $t_path, '&#' ) ) {
 404 			echo 'Can not safely determine $g_path. Please set $g_path manually in ' . $g_config_path . 'config_inc.php';
 405 			die;
 406 		}
 407 	} else {
 408 		$t_path = 'mantisbt/';
 409 	}
 410 
 411 	$g_path	= $t_protocol . '://' . $t_host . $t_path;
 412 	$g_short_path = $t_path;
 413 
 414 	return true;
 415 }

 417 /**
 418  * Define an autoload function to automatically load classes when referenced
 419  *
 420  * @param string $p_class Class name being autoloaded.
 421  * @return void
 422  */
 423 function autoload_mantis( $p_class ) {
 424 	global $g_core_path;
 425 
 426 	# Remove namespace from class name
 427 	$t_end_of_namespace = strrpos( $p_class, '\\' );
 428 	if( $t_end_of_namespace !== false ) {
 429 		$p_class = substr( $p_class, $t_end_of_namespace + 1 );
 430 	}
 431 
 432 	# Commands
 433 	if( substr( $p_class, -7 ) === 'Command' ) {
 434 		$t_require_path = $g_core_path . 'commands/' . $p_class . '.php';
 435 		if( file_exists( $t_require_path ) ) {
 436 			require_once( $t_require_path );
 437 			return;
 438 		}
 439 	}
 440 
 441 	# Exceptions
 442 	if( substr( $p_class, -9 ) === 'Exception' ) {
 443 		$t_require_path = $g_core_path . 'exceptions/' . $p_class . '.php';
 444 		if( file_exists( $t_require_path ) ) {
 445 			require_once( $t_require_path );
 446 			return;
 447 		}
 448 	}
 449 
 450 	global $g_class_path;
 451 	global $g_library_path;
 452 
 453 	$t_require_path = $g_class_path . $p_class . '.class.php';
 454 
 455 	if( file_exists( $t_require_path ) ) {
 456 		require_once( $t_require_path );
 457 		return;
 458 	}
 459 
 460 	$t_require_path = $g_library_path . 'rssbuilder/class.' . $p_class . '.inc.php';
 461 
 462 	if( file_exists( $t_require_path ) ) {
 463 		require_once( $t_require_path );
 464 		return;
 465 	}
 466 }

 468 /**
 469  * Ensures the given extension is loaded, dies with an error message if not.
 470  *
 471  * @param string $p_extension      Extension name
 472  * @param string $p_reason_message Justification for requiring the extension
 473  * @return bool
 474  */
 475 function ensure_php_extension_loaded( $p_extension, $p_reason_message ) {
 476 	if( extension_loaded( $p_extension ) ) {
 477 		return true;
 478 	}
 479 
 480 	/** @noinspection HtmlUnknownTarget */
 481 	printf( '<strong>FATAL ERROR: PHP <i>%1$s</i> extension is not enabled.</strong><br>'
 482 		. 'MantisBT requires this extension %2$s.<br>'
 483 		. '<a href="%3$s">%3$s</a>',
 484 		$p_extension,
 485 		$p_reason_message,
 486 		"https://www.php.net/manual/en/$p_extension.installation.php"
 487 	);
 488 	die;
 489 }

  68 /**
  69  * Function to be called when a user is attempting to access a page that
  70  * he/she is not authorised to.  This outputs an access denied message then
  71  * re-directs to the mainpage.
  72  *
  73  * @return void
  74  * @throws ClientException
  75  */
  76 function access_denied() {
  77 	$t_return = '';
  78 	if( basename( $_SERVER['SCRIPT_NAME'] ) != auth_login_page() ) {
  79 		$t_return_page = $_SERVER['SCRIPT_NAME'];
  80 		if( isset( $_SERVER['QUERY_STRING'] ) && !is_blank( $_SERVER['QUERY_STRING'] ) ) {
  81 			$t_return_page .= '?' . $_SERVER['QUERY_STRING'];
  82 		}
  83 		$t_return = [ 'return' => string_sanitize_url( $t_return_page ) ];
  84 	}
  85 
  86 	if( !auth_is_user_authenticated() ) {
  87 		print_header_redirect( helper_mantis_url( auth_login_page( $t_return ) ), false, false, true );
  88 	} else {
  89 		$t_buttons = [];
  90 		
  91 		# Login button
  92 		if( current_user_is_anonymous() ) {
  93 			$t_buttons[] = [
  94 				helper_mantis_url( auth_login_page( $t_return ) ),
  95 				lang_get( 'login' )
  96 			];
  97 		}
  98 
  99 		# Proceed button
 100 		$t_buttons[] = [
 101 			helper_mantis_url( config_get_global( 'default_home_page' ) ),
 102 			lang_get( 'proceed' )
 103 		];
 104 
 105 		http_response_code( HTTP_STATUS_FORBIDDEN );
 106 		html_robots_noindex();
 107 		layout_page_header();
 108 		layout_page_begin();
 109 		html_operation_confirmation( $t_buttons,
 110 			error_string( ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED ), CONFIRMATION_TYPE_FAILURE );
 111 		layout_page_end();
 112 	}
 113 	http_response_code(HTTP_STATUS_FORBIDDEN);
 114 	exit(1);
 115 }

 117 /**
 118  * retrieves and returns access matrix for a project from cache or caching if required.
 119  * @param integer $p_project_id Integer representing project identifier.
 120  * @return array returns an array of users->accesslevel for the given user
 121  * @access private
 122  */
 123 function access_cache_matrix_project( $p_project_id ) {
 124 	global $g_cache_access_matrix, $g_cache_access_matrix_project_ids;
 125 
 126 	if( ALL_PROJECTS == (int)$p_project_id ) {
 127 		return array();
 128 	}
 129 
 130 	if( !in_array( (int)$p_project_id, $g_cache_access_matrix_project_ids ) ) {
 131 		db_param_push();
 132 		$t_query = 'SELECT user_id, access_level FROM {project_user_list} WHERE project_id=' . db_param();
 133 		$t_result = db_query( $t_query, array( (int)$p_project_id ) );
 134 		while( $t_row = db_fetch_array( $t_result ) ) {
 135 			$g_cache_access_matrix[(int)$t_row['user_id']][(int)$p_project_id] = (int)$t_row['access_level'];
 136 		}
 137 
 138 		$g_cache_access_matrix_project_ids[] = (int)$p_project_id;
 139 	}
 140 
 141 	$t_results = array();
 142 
 143 	foreach( $g_cache_access_matrix as $t_user ) {
 144 		if( isset( $t_user[(int)$p_project_id] ) ) {
 145 			$t_results[(int)$p_project_id] = $t_user[(int)$p_project_id];
 146 		}
 147 	}
 148 
 149 	return $t_results;
 150 }

 152 /**
 153  * retrieves and returns access matrix for a user from cache or caching if required.
 154  * @param integer $p_user_id Integer representing user identifier.
 155  * @return array returns an array of projects->accesslevel for the given user
 156  * @access private
 157  */
 158 function access_cache_matrix_user( $p_user_id ) {
 159 	global $g_cache_access_matrix, $g_cache_access_matrix_user_ids;
 160 
 161 	if( !in_array( (int)$p_user_id, $g_cache_access_matrix_user_ids ) ) {
 162 		db_param_push();
 163 		$t_query = 'SELECT project_id, access_level FROM {project_user_list} WHERE user_id=' . db_param();
 164 		$t_result = db_query( $t_query, array( (int)$p_user_id ) );
 165 
 166 		# make sure we always have an array to return
 167 		$g_cache_access_matrix[(int)$p_user_id] = array();
 168 
 169 		while( $t_row = db_fetch_array( $t_result ) ) {
 170 			$g_cache_access_matrix[(int)$p_user_id][(int)$t_row['project_id']] = (int)$t_row['access_level'];
 171 		}

 174 	}

 176 	return $g_cache_access_matrix[(int)$p_user_id];

 179 /**
 180  * Check the a user's access against the given "threshold" and return true
 181  * if the user can access, false otherwise.
 182  * $p_threshold may be a single value, or an array. If it is a single
 183  * value, treat it as a threshold so return true if user is >= threshold.
 184  * If it is an array, look for exact matches to one of the values
 185  * @param integer       $p_user_access_level User access level.
 186  * @param integer|array $p_threshold         Access threshold, defaults to NOBODY.
 187  * @return boolean true or false depending on whether given access level matches the threshold
 188  * @access public
 189  */
 190 function access_compare_level( $p_user_access_level, $p_threshold = NOBODY ) {
 191 	if( is_array( $p_threshold ) ) {
 192 		return( in_array( $p_user_access_level, $p_threshold ) );
 193 	} else {
 194 		return( $p_user_access_level >= $p_threshold );
 195 	}
 196 }

 198 /**
 199  * This function only checks the user's global access level, ignoring any
 200  * overrides they might have at a project level
 201  * @param integer|null $p_user_id Integer representing user identifier, defaults to null to use current user.
 202  * @return integer global access level
 203  * @access public
 204  */
 205 function access_get_global_level( $p_user_id = null ) {
 206 	if( $p_user_id === null ) {
 207 		$p_user_id = auth_get_current_user_id();
 208 	}
 209 
 210 	# Deal with not logged in silently in this case
 211 	# @@@ we may be able to remove this and just error
 212 	#     and once we default to anon login, we can remove it for sure
 213 	if( empty( $p_user_id ) && !auth_is_user_authenticated() ) {
 214 		return false;
 215 	}
 216 
 217 	return (int)user_get_field( $p_user_id, 'access_level' );
 218 }

 220 /**
 221  * Check the current user's access against the given value and return true
 222  * if the user's access is equal to or higher, false otherwise.
 223  * @param integer      $p_access_level Integer representing access level.
 224  * @param integer|null $p_user_id      Integer representing user id, defaults to null to use current user.
 225  * @return boolean whether user has access level specified
 226  * @access public
 227  */
 228 function access_has_global_level( $p_access_level, $p_user_id = null ) {
 229 	# Short circuit the check in this case
 230 	if( NOBODY == $p_access_level ) {
 231 		return false;
 232 	}
 233 
 234 	$t_access_level = access_get_global_level( $p_user_id );
 235 
 236 	return access_compare_level( $t_access_level, $p_access_level );
 237 }

 239 /**
 240  * Check if the user has the specified global access level
 241  * and deny access to the page if not
 242  * @see access_has_global_level
 243  * @param integer      $p_access_level Integer representing access level.
 244  * @param integer|null $p_user_id      Integer representing user id, defaults to null to use current user.
 245  * @access public
 246  * @return void
 247  */
 248 function access_ensure_global_level( $p_access_level, $p_user_id = null ) {
 249 	if( !access_has_global_level( $p_access_level, $p_user_id ) ) {
 250 		access_denied();
 251 	}
 252 }

 254 /**
 255  * This function checks the project access level first (for the current project
 256  * if none is specified) and if the user is not listed, it falls back on the
 257  * user's global access level.
 258  * @param integer      $p_project_id Integer representing project id to check access against.
 259  * @param integer|null $p_user_id    Integer representing user id, defaults to null to use current user.
 260  * @return integer access level user has to given project
 261  * @access public
 262  */
 263 function access_get_project_level( $p_project_id = null, $p_user_id = null ) {
 264 	if( null === $p_user_id ) {
 265 		$p_user_id = auth_get_current_user_id();
 266 	}
 267 
 268 	# Deal with not logged in silently in this case
 269 	# @todo we may be able to remove this and just error and once we default to anon login, we can remove it for sure
 270 	if( empty( $p_user_id ) && !auth_is_user_authenticated() ) {
 271 		return ANYBODY;
 272 	}
 273 
 274 	if( null === $p_project_id ) {
 275 		$p_project_id = helper_get_current_project();
 276 	}
 277 
 278 	$t_global_access_level = access_get_global_level( $p_user_id );
 279 
 280 	if( ALL_PROJECTS == $p_project_id || user_is_administrator( $p_user_id ) ) {
 281 		return $t_global_access_level;
 282 	} else {
 283 		$t_project_access_level = access_get_local_level( $p_user_id, $p_project_id );
 284 		$t_project_view_state = project_get_field( $p_project_id, 'view_state' );
 285 
 286 		# Try to use the project access level.
 287 		# If the user is not listed in the project, then try to fall back
 288 		#  to the global access level
 289 		if( false === $t_project_access_level ) {
 290 			# If the project is private and the user isn't listed, then they
 291 			# must have the private_project_threshold access level to get in.
 292 			if( VS_PRIVATE == $t_project_view_state ) {
 293 				if( access_compare_level( $t_global_access_level, config_get( 'private_project_threshold', null, null, ALL_PROJECTS ) ) ) {
 294 					return $t_global_access_level;
 295 				} else {
 296 					return ANYBODY;
 297 				}
 298 			} else {
 299 				# project access not set, but the project is public
 300 				return $t_global_access_level;
 301 			}
 302 		} else {
 303 			# project specific access was set
 304 			return $t_project_access_level;
 305 		}
 306 	}
 307 }
 308 
 309 /**
 310  * Check the current user's access against the given value and return true
 311  * if the user's access is equal to or higher, false otherwise.
 312  * @param integer|array $p_access_level Threshold representing an access level.
 313  * @param integer       $p_project_id   Integer representing project id to check access against.
 314  * @param integer|null  $p_user_id      Integer representing user id, defaults to null to use current user.
 315  * @return boolean whether user has access level specified
 316  * @access public
 317  */
 318 function access_has_project_level( $p_access_level, $p_project_id = null, $p_user_id = null ) {
 319 	# Short circuit the check in this case
 320 	if( NOBODY == $p_access_level ) {
 321 		return false;
 322 	}
 323 
 324 	if( null === $p_user_id ) {
 325 		$p_user_id = auth_get_current_user_id();
 326 	}
 327 	if( null === $p_project_id ) {
 328 		$p_project_id = helper_get_current_project();
 329 	}
 330 
 331 	$t_access_level = access_get_project_level( $p_project_id, $p_user_id );
 332 
 333 	return access_compare_level( $t_access_level, $p_access_level );
 334 }

 336 /**
 337  * Filters an array of project ids based on an access level.
 338  *
 339  * Returns an array containing only those projects which meet said access level.
 340  * An optional limit for the number of results is provided as a shortcut for
 341  * access checks.
 342  *
 343  * @param integer|array|string  $p_access_level Parameter representing access level threshold, may be:
 344  *                                              - integer: for a simple threshold
 345  *                                              - array: for an array threshold
 346  *                                              - string: for a threshold option which will be evaluated
 347  *                                                for each project context
 348  * @param array|null            $p_project_ids  Array of project ids to check access against, default to null
 349  *                                               to use all user accessible projects
 350  * @param integer|null          $p_user_id      Integer representing user id, defaults to null to use current user.
 351  * @param integer               $p_limit        Maximum number of results, default is 0 for all results
 352  *
 353  * @return array                The filtered array of project ids
 354  */
 355 function access_project_array_filter( $p_access_level, ?array $p_project_ids = null, ?int $p_user_id = null, int $p_limit = 0 ): array {
 356 	# Short circuit the check in this case
 357 	if( NOBODY == $p_access_level ) {
 358 		return array();
 359 	}
 360 
 361 	if( null === $p_user_id ) {
 362 		$p_user_id = auth_get_current_user_id();
 363 	}
 364 	if( null === $p_project_ids ) {
 365 		$p_project_ids = user_get_all_accessible_projects( $p_user_id );
 366 	}
 367 
 368 	# Determine if parameter is a configuration string to be evaluated for each project
 369 	$t_is_config_string = ( is_string( $p_access_level ) && !is_numeric( $p_access_level ) );
 370 
 371 	# if config will be evaluated for each project, prepare a default value
 372 	if( $t_is_config_string ) {
 373 		$t_default = config_get( $p_access_level, null, $p_user_id, ALL_PROJECTS );
 374 		if( null === $t_default ) {
 375 			$t_default = config_get_global( $p_access_level );
 376 		}
 377 	}
 378 
 379 	project_cache_array_rows( $p_project_ids );
 380 
 381 	$t_check_level = $p_access_level;
 382 	$t_filtered_projects = array();
 383 	foreach( $p_project_ids as $t_project_id ) {
 384 		# If a config string is provided, evaluate for each project
 385 		if( $t_is_config_string ) {
 386 			$t_check_level = config_get( $p_access_level, $t_default, $p_user_id, $t_project_id );
 387 		}
 388 		if( access_has_project_level( $t_check_level, $t_project_id, $p_user_id ) ) {
 389 			$t_filtered_projects[] = $t_project_id;
 390 			# Shortcut if the result limit has been reached
 391 			if( --$p_limit == 0 ) {
 392 				break;
 393 			}
 394 		}
 395 	}
 396 
 397 	return $t_filtered_projects;
 398 }
 399 
 400 /**
 401  * Check if the user has access to at least one of the specified projects.
 402  *
 403  * Check the current user's access against the given value, in each of the
 404  * provided projects, and return true if the user's access is equal to or
 405  * higher in any of the projects, false otherwise.
 406  *
 407  * @param int|array|string $p_access_level Access level threshold, may be:
 408  *                                         - integer: for a simple threshold
 409  *                                         - array: for an array threshold
 410  *                                         - string: for a threshold option to be
 411  *                                           evaluated in each project's context.
 412  * @param array|null       $p_project_ids  Array of project ids to check access against,
 413  *                                         to use all user accessible projects.
 414  * @param int|null         $p_user_id      User id, defaults to null to use current user.
 415  *
 416  * @return bool            True if user has the specified access level in any of the projects.
 417  * @access public
 418  */
 419 function access_has_any_project_level( $p_access_level, ?array $p_project_ids = null, ?int $p_user_id = null ): bool {
 420 	# We only need 1 matching project to return positive
 421 	$t_matches = access_project_array_filter( $p_access_level, $p_project_ids, $p_user_id, 1 );
 422 	return !empty( $t_matches );
 423 }

 456 /**
 457  * Check whether the user has the specified access level for any project project
 458  *
 459  * Warning: this function may mislead into incorrect validations. Usually you want to
 460  * check that a user meets a threshold for any project, but that threshold may be configured
 461  * differently for each project, and the user may also have different access levels in each
 462  * project due to private projects assignment.
 463  * In that scenario, $p_access_level can't be a static threshold, but a "threshold identifier"
 464  * instead, that must be evaluated for each project.
 465  * Function "access_has_any_project_level()" provides that functionality, also covers the basic
 466  * usage of this function.
 467  * For such reasons, this function has been deprecated.
 468  *
 469  * @param integer      $p_access_level Integer representing access level.
 470  * @param integer|null $p_user_id      Integer representing user id, defaults to null to use current user.
 471  * @return boolean whether user has access level specified
 472  * @access public
 473  * @deprecated	access_has_any_project_level() should be used in preference to this function (since verrsion 2.6)
 474  */
 475 function access_has_any_project( $p_access_level, $p_user_id = null ) {
 476 	error_parameters( __FUNCTION__ . '()', 'access_has_any_project_level()' );
 477 	trigger_error( ERROR_DEPRECATED_SUPERSEDED, DEPRECATED );
 478 
 479 	# Short circuit the check in this case
 480 	if( NOBODY == $p_access_level ) {
 481 		return false;
 482 	}
 483 
 484 	if( null === $p_user_id ) {
 485 		$p_user_id = auth_get_current_user_id();
 486 	}
 487 
 488 	$t_projects = project_get_all_rows();
 489 	foreach( $t_projects as $t_project ) {
 490 		if( access_has_project_level( $p_access_level, $t_project['id'], $p_user_id ) ) {
 491 			return true;
 492 		}
 493 	}
 494 
 495 	return false;
 496 }
 497 
 498 /**
 499  * Check the current user's access against the given value and return true
 500  * if the user's access is equal to or higher, false otherwise.
 501  * This function looks up the bug's project and performs an access check
 502  * against that project
 503  * @param integer      $p_access_level Integer representing access level.
 504  * @param integer      $p_bug_id       Integer representing bug id to check access against.
 505  * @param integer|null $p_user_id      Integer representing user id, defaults to null to use current user.
 506  * @return boolean whether user has access level specified
 507  * @access public
 508  */
 509 function access_has_bug_level( $p_access_level, $p_bug_id, $p_user_id = null ) {
 510 	if( $p_user_id === null ) {
 511 		$p_user_id = auth_get_current_user_id();
 512 	}
 513 
 514 	# Deal with not logged in silently in this case
 515 	# @@@ we may be able to remove this and just error
 516 	#     and once we default to anon login, we can remove it for sure
 517 	if( empty( $p_user_id ) && !auth_is_user_authenticated() ) {
 518 		return false;
 519 	}
 520 
 521 	# Check the requested access level, shortcut to fail if not satisfied
 522 	$t_project_id = bug_get_field( $p_bug_id, 'project_id' );
 523 	$t_access_level = access_get_project_level( $t_project_id, $p_user_id );
 524 	if( !access_compare_level( $t_access_level, $p_access_level ) ){
 525 		return false;
 526 	}
 527 
 528 	# If the level is met, we still need to verify that user has access to the issue
 529 
 530 	# Check if the bug is private
 531 	$t_bug_is_user_reporter = bug_is_user_reporter( $p_bug_id, $p_user_id );
 532 	if( !$t_bug_is_user_reporter && bug_get_field( $p_bug_id, 'view_state' ) == VS_PRIVATE ) {
 533 		$t_private_bug_threshold = config_get( 'private_bug_threshold', null, $p_user_id, $t_project_id );
 534 		if( !access_compare_level( $t_access_level, $t_private_bug_threshold ) ) {
 535 			return false;
 536 		}
 537 	}
 538 
 539 	# Check special limits
 540 	# Limited view means this user can only view the issues they reported, is handling, or monitoring
 541 	if( access_has_limited_view( $t_project_id, $p_user_id ) ) {
 542 		$t_allowed = $t_bug_is_user_reporter;
 543 		if( !$t_allowed ) {
 544 			$t_allowed = bug_is_user_handler( $p_bug_id, $p_user_id );
 545 		}
 546 		if( !$t_allowed ) {
 547 			$t_allowed = user_is_monitoring_bug( $p_user_id, $p_bug_id );
 548 		}
 549 		if( !$t_allowed ) {
 550 			return false;
 551 		}
 552 	}
 553 
 554 	return true;
 555 }

 569 			$t_users_ids_with_access[] = $t_user_id;

 592 /**
 593  * Check the current user's access against the given value and return true
 594  * if the user's access is equal to or higher, false otherwise.
 595  * This function looks up the bugnote's bug and performs an access check
 596  * against that bug
 597  * @param integer      $p_access_level Integer representing access level.
 598  * @param integer      $p_bugnote_id   Integer representing bugnote id to check access against.
 599  * @param integer|null $p_user_id      Integer representing user id, defaults to null to use current user.
 600  * @return boolean whether user has access level specified
 601  * @access public
 602  */
 603 function access_has_bugnote_level( $p_access_level, $p_bugnote_id, $p_user_id = null ) {
 604 	if( null === $p_user_id ) {
 605 		$p_user_id = auth_get_current_user_id();
 606 	}
 607 
 608 	$t_bug_id = bugnote_get_field( $p_bugnote_id, 'bug_id' );
 609 	$t_project_id = bug_get_field( $t_bug_id, 'project_id' );
 610 
 611 	# If the bug is private and the user is not the reporter, then the
 612 	# the user must also have higher access than private_bug_threshold
 613 	if( bugnote_get_field( $p_bugnote_id, 'view_state' ) == VS_PRIVATE && !bugnote_is_user_reporter( $p_bugnote_id, $p_user_id ) ) {
 614 		$t_private_bugnote_threshold = config_get( 'private_bugnote_threshold', null, $p_user_id, $t_project_id );
 615 		$p_access_level = max( $p_access_level, $t_private_bugnote_threshold );
 616 	}
 617 
 618 	return access_has_bug_level( $p_access_level, $t_bug_id, $p_user_id );
 619 }

 656 /**
 657  * Check if the specified bug can be closed
 658  * @param BugData      $p_bug     Bug to check access against.
 659  * @param integer|null $p_user_id Integer representing user id, defaults to null to use current user.
 660  * @return boolean true if user can close the bug
 661  * @access public
 662  */
 663 function access_can_close_bug( BugData $p_bug, $p_user_id = null ) {
 664 	if( bug_is_closed( $p_bug->id ) ) {
 665 		# Can't close a bug that's already closed
 666 		return false;
 667 	}
 668 
 669 	if( null === $p_user_id ) {
 670 		$p_user_id = auth_get_current_user_id();
 671 	}
 672 
 673 	# If allow_reporter_close is enabled, then reporters can close their own bugs
 674 	# if they are in resolved status
 675 	if( ON == config_get( 'allow_reporter_close', null, null, $p_bug->project_id )
 676 		&& bug_is_user_reporter( $p_bug->id, $p_user_id )
 677 		&& bug_is_resolved( $p_bug->id )
 678 	) {
 679 		return true;
 680 	}
 681 
 682 	$t_closed_status = config_get( 'bug_closed_status_threshold', null, null, $p_bug->project_id );
 683 	$t_closed_status_threshold = access_get_status_threshold( $t_closed_status, $p_bug->project_id );
 684 	return access_has_bug_level( $t_closed_status_threshold, $p_bug->id, $p_user_id );
 685 }

 697 		access_denied();
 698 	}

 701 /**
 702  * Check if the specified bug can be reopened
 703  * @param BugData      $p_bug     Bug to check access against.
 704  * @param integer|null $p_user_id Integer representing user id, defaults to null to use current user.
 705  * @return boolean whether user has access to reopen bugs
 706  * @access public
 707  */
 708 function access_can_reopen_bug( BugData $p_bug, $p_user_id = null ) {
 709 	if( !bug_is_resolved( $p_bug->id ) ) {
 710 		# Can't reopen a bug that's not resolved
 711 		return false;
 712 	}
 713 
 714 	if( $p_user_id === null ) {
 715 		$p_user_id = auth_get_current_user_id();
 716 	}
 717 
 718 	$t_reopen_status = config_get( 'bug_reopen_status', null, null, $p_bug->project_id );
 719 
 720 	# Reopen status must be reachable by workflow
 721 	if( !bug_check_workflow( $p_bug->status, $t_reopen_status ) ) {
 722 		return false;
 723 	}
 724 
 725 	# If allow_reporter_reopen is enabled, then reporters can always reopen
 726 	# their own bugs as long as their access level is reporter or above
 727 	if( ON == config_get( 'allow_reporter_reopen', null, null, $p_bug->project_id )
 728 		&& bug_is_user_reporter( $p_bug->id, $p_user_id )
 729 		&& access_has_project_level( config_get( 'report_bug_threshold', null, $p_user_id, $p_bug->project_id ), $p_bug->project_id, $p_user_id )
 730 	) {
 731 		return true;
 732 	}
 733 
 734 	# Other users's access level must allow them to reopen bugs
 735 	$t_reopen_bug_threshold = config_get( 'reopen_bug_threshold', null, null, $p_bug->project_id );
 736 	if( access_has_bug_level( $t_reopen_bug_threshold, $p_bug->id, $p_user_id ) ) {
 737 
 738 		# User must be allowed to change status to reopen status
 739 		$t_reopen_status_threshold = access_get_status_threshold( $t_reopen_status, $p_bug->project_id );
 740 		return access_has_bug_level( $t_reopen_status_threshold, $p_bug->id, $p_user_id );
 741 	}
 742 
 743 	return false;
 744 }

 749  * @see access_can_reopen_bug

 755 function access_ensure_can_reopen_bug( BugData $p_bug, $p_user_id = null ) {

 761 /**
 762  * get the user's access level specific to this project.
 763  * return false (0) if the user has no access override here
 764  * @param integer $p_user_id    Integer representing user id.
 765  * @param integer $p_project_id Integer representing project id.
 766  * @return boolean|integer returns false (if no access) or an integer representing level of access
 767  * @access public
 768  */
 769 function access_get_local_level( $p_user_id, $p_project_id ) {
 770 	global $g_cache_access_matrix, $g_cache_access_matrix_project_ids;
 771 
 772 	$p_project_id = (int)$p_project_id;
 773 	$p_user_id = (int)$p_user_id;
 774 
 775 	if( in_array( $p_project_id, $g_cache_access_matrix_project_ids ) ) {
 776 		if( isset( $g_cache_access_matrix[$p_user_id][$p_project_id] ) ) {
 777 			return $g_cache_access_matrix[$p_user_id][$p_project_id];
 778 		} else {
 779 			return false;
 780 		}
 781 	}
 782 
 783 	$t_project_level = access_cache_matrix_user( $p_user_id );
 784 
 785 	if( isset( $t_project_level[$p_project_id] ) ) {
 786 		return $t_project_level[$p_project_id];
 787 	} else {
 788 		return false;
 789 	}
 790 }

 792 /**
 793  * get the access level required to change the issue to the new status
 794  * If there is no specific differentiated access level, use the
 795  * generic update_bug_status_threshold.
 796  * @param integer $p_status     Status.
 797  * @param integer $p_project_id Default value ALL_PROJECTS.
 798  * @return integer integer representing user level e.g. DEVELOPER
 799  * @access public
 800  */
 801 function access_get_status_threshold( $p_status, $p_project_id = ALL_PROJECTS ) {
 802 	$t_thresh_array = config_get( 'set_status_threshold', null, null, $p_project_id );
 803 	if( isset( $t_thresh_array[(int)$p_status] ) ) {
 804 		return (int)$t_thresh_array[(int)$p_status];
 805 	} else {
 806 		if( $p_status == config_get( 'bug_submit_status', null, null, $p_project_id ) ) {
 807 			return config_get( 'report_bug_threshold', null, null, $p_project_id );
 808 		} else {
 809 			return config_get( 'update_bug_status_threshold', null, null, $p_project_id );
 810 		}
 811 	}
 812 }

 814 /**
 815  * Given a access level, return the appropriate string for it
 816  * @param integer $p_access_level
 817  * @return string
 818  */
 819 function access_level_get_string( $p_access_level ) {
 820 	if( $p_access_level > ANYBODY ) {
 821 		$t_access_level_string = get_enum_element( 'access_levels', $p_access_level );
 822 	} else {
 823 		$t_access_level_string = lang_get( 'no_access' );
 824 	}
 825 	return $t_access_level_string;
 826 }

 828 /**
 829  * Return the minimum access level, as integer, that matches the threshold.
 830  * $p_threshold may be a single value, or an array. If it is a single
 831  * value, returns that number. If it is an array, return the value of the
 832  * smallest element
 833  * @param integer|array $p_threshold         Access threshold
 834  * @return integer		Integer value for an access level.
 835  */
 836 function access_threshold_min_level( $p_threshold ) {
 837 	if( is_array( $p_threshold ) ) {
 838 		if( empty( $p_threshold ) ) {
 839 			return NOBODY;
 840 		} else {
 841 			sort( $p_threshold );
 842 			return( reset( $p_threshold ) );
 843 		}
 844 	} else {
 845 		return $p_threshold;
 846 	}
 847 
 848 }

 850 /**
 851  * Checks if the user can view the handler for the bug.
 852  * @param BugData      $p_bug     Bug to check access against.
 853  * @param integer|null $p_user_id Integer representing user id, defaults to null to use current user.
 854  * @return boolean whether user can view the handler user.
 855  */
 856 function access_can_see_handler_for_bug( BugData $p_bug, $p_user_id = null ) {
 857 	if( null === $p_user_id ) {
 858 		$t_user_id = auth_get_current_user_id();
 859 	} else {
 860 		$t_user_id = $p_user_id;
 861 	}
 862 
 863 	# handler can be viewed if allowed by access level, OR the user himself is the handler
 864 	$t_can_view_handler =
 865 		( $p_bug->handler_id == $t_user_id )
 866 		|| access_has_bug_level(
 867 			config_get( 'view_handler_threshold', null, $t_user_id, $p_bug->project_id ),
 868 			$p_bug->id );
 869 
 870 	return $t_can_view_handler;
 871 }

 873 /**
 874  * Parse access level reference array parsed from json.
 875  *
 876  * @param array $p_access The access level
 877  * @return integer The access level
 878  * @throws ClientException Access level is invalid or not specified.
 879  */
 880 function access_parse_array( array $p_access ) {
 881 	$t_access_levels_enum = config_get( 'access_levels_enum_string' );
 882 	$t_access_level = false;
 883 
 884 	if( isset( $p_access['id'] ) ) {
 885 		$t_access_level = (int)$p_access['id'];
 886 
 887 		# Make sure the provided id is valid
 888 		if( !MantisEnum::hasValue( $t_access_levels_enum, $t_access_level ) ) {
 889 			$t_access_level = false;
 890 		}
 891 	}
 892 
 893 	if( isset( $p_access['name'] ) ) {
 894 		$t_access_level = MantisEnum::getValue( $t_access_levels_enum, $p_access['name'] );
 895 	}
 896 
 897 	if( $t_access_level === false ) {
 898 		throw new ClientException(
 899 			'Invalid access level',
 900 			ERROR_INVALID_FIELD_VALUE,
 901 			array( 'access_level' ) );
 902 	}
 903 
 904 	return $t_access_level;
 905 }
 906 
 907 /**
 908  * Returns true if the user has limited view to issues in the specified project.
 909  *
 910  * @param integer $p_project_id   Project id, or null for current project
 911  * @param integer $p_user_id      User id, or null for current user
 912  * @return boolean	Whether limited view applies
 913  *
 914  * @see $g_limit_view_unless_threshold
 915  * @see $g_limit_reporters
 916  */
 917 function access_has_limited_view( $p_project_id = null, $p_user_id = null ) {
 918 	$t_user_id = ( null === $p_user_id ) ? auth_get_current_user_id() : $p_user_id;
 919 	$t_project_id = ( null === $p_project_id ) ? helper_get_current_project() : $p_project_id;
 920 
 921 	# Old 'limit_reporters' option was previously only supported for ALL_PROJECTS,
 922 	# Use this option if set, otherwise, check the new option for "unlimited view" threshold
 923 	$t_old_limit_reporters = config_get( 'limit_reporters', null, $t_user_id, ALL_PROJECTS );
 924 	$t_threshold_can_view = NOBODY;
 925 	if( ON != $t_old_limit_reporters ) {
 926 		$t_threshold_can_view = config_get( 'limit_view_unless_threshold', null, $t_user_id, $t_project_id );
 927 	} else {
 928 		# If old 'limit_reporters' option is enabled, use that setting
 929 		# Note that the effective threshold can vary for each project, based on
 930 		# the reporting threshold configuration.
 931 		# To improve performance, esp. when processing for several projects, we
 932 		# build a static array holding that threshold for each project
 933 		static $s_thresholds = array();
 934 		if( !isset( $s_thresholds[$t_project_id] ) ) {
 935 			$t_report_bug_threshold = config_get( 'report_bug_threshold', null, $t_user_id, $t_project_id );
 936 			if( empty( $t_report_bug_threshold ) ) {
 937 				$s_thresholds[$t_project_id] = NOBODY;
 938 			} else {
 939 				$s_thresholds[$t_project_id] = access_threshold_min_level( $t_report_bug_threshold ) + 1;
 940 			}
 941 		}
 942 		$t_threshold_can_view = $s_thresholds[$t_project_id];
 943 	}
 944 
 945 	$t_project_level = access_get_project_level( $p_project_id, $p_user_id );
 946 	return !access_compare_level( $t_project_level, $t_threshold_can_view );
 947 }
 948 
 949 /**
 950  * Return true if user is allowed to view bug revisions.
 951  *
 952  * User must have $g_bug_revision_view_threshold or be the bug's reporter.
 953  *
 954  * @param int $p_bug_id
 955  * @param int $p_user_id
 956  *
 957  * @return bool
 958  */
 959 function access_can_view_bug_revisions( $p_bug_id, $p_user_id = null ) {
 960 	if( !bug_exists( $p_bug_id ) ) {
 961 		return false;
 962 	}
 963 	$t_project_id = bug_get_field( $p_bug_id, 'project_id' );
 964 	$t_user_id = null === $p_user_id ? auth_get_current_user_id() : $p_user_id;
 965 
 966 	$t_has_access = access_has_bug_level(
 967 		config_get( 'bug_revision_view_threshold', null, $t_user_id, $t_project_id ),
 968 		$p_bug_id,
 969 		$t_user_id
 970 	);
 971 
 972 	return $t_has_access || bug_is_user_reporter( $p_bug_id, $t_user_id );
 973 }
 974 
 975 /**
 976  * Return true if user is allowed to view bugnote revisions.
 977  *
 978  * User must have $g_bug_revision_view_threshold or be the bugnote's reporter.
 979  *
 980  * @param int $p_bugnote_id
 981  * @param int $p_user_id
 982  *
 983  * @return bool
 984  */
 985 function access_can_view_bugnote_revisions( $p_bugnote_id, $p_user_id = null ) {
 986 	if( !bugnote_exists( $p_bugnote_id ) ) {
 987 		return false;
 988 	}
 989 	$t_bug_id = bugnote_get_field( $p_bugnote_id, 'bug_id' );
 990 	$t_project_id = bug_get_field( $t_bug_id, 'project_id' );
 991 	$t_user_id = null === $p_user_id ? auth_get_current_user_id() : $p_user_id;
 992 
 993 	$t_has_access = access_has_bugnote_level(
 994 		config_get( 'bug_revision_view_threshold', null, $t_user_id, $t_project_id ),
 995 		$p_bugnote_id,
 996 		$t_user_id
 997 	);
 998 
 999 
1000 	return $t_has_access || bugnote_is_user_reporter( $p_bugnote_id, $t_user_id );
1001 }

  17 require_api( 'access_api.php' );
  18 require_api( 'history_api.php' );
  19 
  20 use Mantis\Exceptions\ClientException;
  21 
  22 /**
  23  * Antispam API
  24  *
  25  * @package CoreAPI
  26  * @subpackage AntispamAPI
  27  * @copyright Copyright 2015 MantisBT Team - mantisbt-dev@lists.sourceforge.net
  28  * @link http://www.mantisbt.org
  29  *
  30  * @uses access_api.php
  31  * @uses history_api.php
  32  */
  33 
  34 /**
  35  * Triggers an error if the current user is suspected to be a spammer.
  36  * This should be run before actions like adding issues or issue notes. If the
  37  * user is determined to demonstrate spammy behavior, this method will trigger an
  38  * error and exit the script.
  39  */
  40 function antispam_check() {
  41 	if( !auth_signup_enabled() ) {
  42 		return;
  43 	}
  44 
  45 	if( access_get_global_level() > auth_signup_access_level() ) {
  46 		return;
  47 	}
  48 
  49 	$t_antispam_max_event_count = config_get( 'antispam_max_event_count' );
  50 	if( $t_antispam_max_event_count == 0 ) {
  51 		return;
  52 	}
  53 
  54 	# Make sure user has at least one more event to add before exceeding the limit, which will happen
  55 	# after this method returns.
  56 	$t_antispam_time_window_in_seconds = config_get( 'antispam_time_window_in_seconds' );
  57 	if( history_count_user_recent_events( $t_antispam_time_window_in_seconds ) < $t_antispam_max_event_count ) {
  58 		return;
  59 	}
  60 
  61 	throw new ClientException(
  62 		"Hit rate limit threshold",
  63 		ERROR_SPAM_SUSPECTED,
  64 		array( $t_antispam_max_event_count, $t_antispam_time_window_in_seconds )
  65 	);
  66 }

   2 # MantisBT - A PHP based bugtracking system

  12 # GNU General Public License for more details.
  13 #
